rationale: Tests recall of the five major HAI types and their causative agents from the classification table that completes this learning point.
Tests understanding of the sequential chain of HAI transmission — the six links must be ordered correctly to identify effective intervention points.
Tests a clinically critical distinction about ABHR limitations for spore-forming organisms — a common source of student error that this clinical pearl explicitly addresses.
Tests application of transmission-based precaution selection for pulmonary TB — anchored after the block that defines contact, droplet, and airborne precaution categories.
Tests understanding of the primary horizontal gene transfer mechanism for carbapenemase resistance — anchored after the block explaining ESKAPE pathogens and resistance evolution mechanisms.
Tests recall of the WHO handwashing technique steps in correct visual sequence — the technique is inherently visual and commonly examined in clinical skill assessments.
Tests recall of the correct PPE doffing sequence — removing the most contaminated items first is critical for self-contamination prevention, as explicitly taught in the donning and doffing block.
Tests application of BMW Rules 2016 colour-coded segregation to a clinical scenario — anchored after the block defining the four BMW categories and their corresponding bag colours.
Tests application of environmental surveillance methods to a clinical outbreak scenario — anchored after the block explaining water, air, and surface surveillance techniques.
